How many records to judge by hand to show a recall target

Source: R/doc-screen-recall.R
gr_screen_sample_size.Rd

Sizes a reference sample for gr_calibrate() so that, if the sample turns up no missed eligible record, the one-sided bound clears the target at the confidence asked for. One miss or more widens the bound, so treat the result as the least that could be enough.

Usage

gr_screen_sample_size(
  recall_target = 0.95,
  conf = 0.95,
  prevalence = NULL,
  frame = "all",
  max_lost = NULL,
  frame_n = NULL
)

Arguments

recall_target

The recall to show, strictly between 0 and 1. Used by frame = "all"; for the other frames it enters through max_lost.

conf

Confidence level of the one-sided bound.

prevalence

Expected share of eligible records among those drawn, for frame = "all": turns the eligible records needed into records to draw. NULL leaves the record count NA.

frame

"all", "excluded" or "stacked", as in gr_reference().

max_lost

For "excluded" and "stacked": the most eligible records the screener may have excluded while still meeting the target.

frame_n

Number of records in the frame sampled: the excluded records for "excluded" and "stacked", everything screened for "all", where with prevalence it caps the draw at the whole frame.

Value

A one-row data frame: the settings, positives (eligible records needed, for "all"), n (records to draw), n_binomial, n_exact, rule and note.

A sample of everything screened (frame = "all")

Recall is bounded from the eligible records the sample happens to contain. With none of k eligible records missed, the one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bound on recall is alpha^(1/k), where alpha = 1 - conf, so the target T is shown once

k >= ln(alpha) / ln(T)

eligible records have been judged: 29 for T = 0.90, 59 for 0.95 and 299 for 0.99 at 95% confidence (Lewis, Yang and Frieder 2021). Divided by the expected prevalence it gives the number of records to draw (59 / 0.05 = 1180). The ten eligible records 0.6.0 asked for support a lower bound of only 0.74, even with all ten found.

Every kept record plus a sample of the exclusions

With the kept records judged in full (frame = "stacked", or frame = "excluded" for the exclusions sample on its own) recall is K / (K + M), where K is the eligible records kept and M those excluded, so a recall target is a cap on M: with K eligible kept, recall T is met when M is at most floor(K (1 - T) / T). Give that cap as max_lost, using a pilot estimate of K, and the excluded frame's size as frame_n.

The exact size is the smallest n for which a frame holding max_lost + 1 eligible records would show none of them in a sample of n with probability at most alpha, from the hypergeometric distribution. This is the bound gr_calibrate() reports. The binomial version, n >= ln(alpha) / ln(1 - u) with u = max_lost / frame_n (299 for u = 1%), is given beside it; it ignores the finite frame and so asks for a few more records.

A finite frame

For frame = "all", gr_calibrate() bounds a sample smaller than the frame with Clopper-Pearson, which treats the frame as infinite, so the eligible records needed do not fall with the frame's size. When the whole frame is judged, recall is known exactly and is its own bound. So with frame_n given, n is the binomial draw when it fits in the frame, and otherwise frame_n itself: at 95% recall, 95% confidence and 5% prevalence, a frame of 500 records holds about 25 eligible records, fewer than the 59 needed, and only judging all 500 can show the target. n_exact is NA for frame = "all".

References

Lewis, D. D., Yang, E. and Frieder, O. (2021). Certifying one-phase technology-assisted reviews. Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management, 893-902.

Clopper, C. J. and Pearson, E. S. (1934). The use of confidence or fiducial limits illustrated in the case of the binomial. Biometrika 26(4), 404-413.

See also

gr_reference(), gr_calibrate()

Other corpus functions: gr_calibrate(), gr_inventory(), gr_records(), gr_reference(), gr_reference_consensus(), gr_resolve(), gr_search()

Examples

# Eligible records to judge for recall of at least 95%, at 95% confidence.
gr_screen_sample_size(0.95, 0.95)
#>   frame recall_target conf prevalence max_lost frame_n positives  n n_binomial
#> 1   all          0.95 0.95         NA       NA      NA        59 NA         NA
#>   n_exact                                                   rule
#> 1      NA zero misses among the eligible: k >= ln(alpha) / ln(T)
#>                                                                          note
#> 1 Give `prevalence` to turn the eligible records needed into records to draw.

# At 5% prevalence that many eligible records means drawing about 1180.
gr_screen_sample_size(0.95, 0.95, prevalence = 0.05)
#>   frame recall_target conf prevalence max_lost frame_n positives    n
#> 1   all          0.95 0.95       0.05       NA      NA        59 1180
#>   n_binomial n_exact                                                   rule
#> 1       1180      NA zero misses among the eligible: k >= ln(alpha) / ln(T)
#>   note
#> 1 <NA>

# Every kept record judged, 285 of them eligible, and 9000 exclusions: at
# most floor(285 * 0.05 / 0.95) = 15 may have been lost.
gr_screen_sample_size(frame = "stacked", max_lost = 15, frame_n = 9000)
#>     frame recall_target conf prevalence max_lost frame_n positives    n
#> 1 stacked          0.95 0.95         NA       15    9000        NA 1536
#>   n_binomial n_exact
#> 1       1796    1536
#>                                                               rule note
#> 1 zero misses in the excluded sample: hypergeometric, finite frame <NA>
